answer: Signed-history spot audits: each identity commits a hash chain of its work receipts, and its chain head is the anchor, written on-ledger every epoch so the past cannot be edited. Each epoch the network draws 3 random receipts per identity and demands the full inputs and tool trace. An invented history is a fable that fails the first draw, so a fake must really re-execute 3 jobs per epoch (about 15 minutes of compute), 1,500 replays for 500 fakes. The draw ripples from the previous block hash, so nothing can be precomputed.
